name: Behalf.bot - FounderOS
description: A gated coach for early-stage founders. It walks a founder through a fixed sequence of stages, from why and founder fit through audience, pain research, discovery, solution test, positioning, content, validation and traction. Each stage ends in a gate that needs ledger evidence, not self-report. Content (framework cards, concept notes, skills, gate specs, Laya question sets) is markdown and JSON in git; founder state lives in a ledger behind a storage interface. This release adds four auditor skills (Mom Test interview audit, pain tagger and pain-log check, earlyvangelist qualifier, Pain-Dream-Fix checker). Laya does the per-item tagging over its /v1/systemone endpoint, Claude writes the feedback, and every tag a founder accepts or rejects is kept as a fine-tuning label. Without Laya the auditors fall back to a Claude-only audit.

enabled.description: Master switch. Enables the auditor skills and runs setup.sh and validate.sh. Stage coaching skills are not shipped yet.

include_contrib.description: Load community cards from contrib/ in addition to core/. Off by default: the coach loads only core/, and founders never see contrib content unless the operator opts in.

ledger_backend.description: Where founder state is stored. postgres uses the chassis database named by BEHALFBOT_PG_DSN or CHASSIS_PG_DSN (the same variables the chassis already sets). sqlite is for development and tests. Exported as FOUNDER_OS_LEDGER_BACKEND.

ledger_pg_schema.description: Postgres schema the ledger tables live in. The plugin creates it if missing and never reads or writes outside it, so its generic table names (artifacts, labels, audits) cannot collide with other tables in the chassis database. Exported as FOUNDER_OS_PG_SCHEMA.

ledger_sqlite_path.description: SQLite ledger file, used only when ledger_backend is sqlite. Exported as FOUNDER_OS_SQLITE_PATH.

activation._note: Auditor skills are invoked on demand from a founder session; there are no scheduled jobs.

system.name: python3
system.install: apt-get install python3 (Debian) / your platform's package manager
system._explanation: Runs the content lint (validate.sh) and the ledger storage interface. Both are stdlib-only apart from the Postgres driver below.

system.name: psycopg
system.install: pip install psycopg==3.2.3 (already in the chassis image)
system._explanation: Postgres driver for the ledger's Postgres adapter. The chassis image ships psycopg 3.2.3, so setup.sh only checks for it and never installs it. It is a soft dependency: without it the SQLite backend still works, and setup.sh warns instead of failing.

system.name: laya
system.install: Optional. A laya-serve or Ollaya instance reachable over HTTP. Set LAYA_URL (e.g. http://laya:8000), and LAYA_API_KEY if the server requires a bearer token. LAYA_TIMEOUT sets seconds per request (default 20).
system._explanation: The auditors send per-item questions to Laya's /v1/systemone endpoint. It is a soft dependency: with LAYA_URL unset, or the server down or timing out, every auditor returns mode claude-only and Claude does the tagging. Nothing is installed or started from this plugin.
